name: Streaming Accountability And Corporate Governance 11A539E2C7
text: Accountability and Corporate Governance presents the following source proposition: Accountability is best understood as a norm of governance, stipulating particular modes of wielding power and of responses to power in the Hohfeldian sense of this term. This proposition is pertinent to Kaal's source-bound claim that Reforms that increase executive accountability to shareholders and increase shareholder control over executives do not solve the problem of corporate short-term focus. The proposed response is an extension: the relationship should remain limited to the retrieved source proposition and the mapped Kaal claim unless fuller source review supports a broader conclusion.
